España ocupa el puesto 26 del ránking e Italia es el 14. "Me siento genial. Tuvimos una gran noche tanto con los pitchers como en el bateo", expuso el técnico. La selección nacional, un ejemplo de la sociedad española del siglo XXI donde se mezclan jugadores nacidos en nuestro país como Jorge Balboa (40 años); Stevens (37), de origen cubano; Andrés Angulo (29), de Colombia, el joven Ernesto Garavito, nacido en Venezuela, o Edgar Rondón y Ramón Rossó, de República Dominicana, afrontará el torneo del año próximo -ampliado a 16 selecciones- en Taiwán y Japón. También habrá en juego una plaza para Asia. "Estoy muy feliz. Hicimos, junto al Ayuntamiento de Barcelona y el CSD, la apuesta de organizar el clasificatorio y nos ha salido bien", apunta Pablo Carpio, el presidente de la Federación Española. "El objetivo real es clasificarnos para los Juegos. Vamos a por ello con todo. No descartamos nada. Hemos ganado el Europeo en 2023 y todo puede pasar. No vamos de outsider". Carpio muestra su orgullo por el combinado construido. "Muchos son de origen latino, pero muchos se han formado aquí. Hay un gran arraigo. No entiendo este tipo de debates. Nosotros estamos encantados de que nuestros jugadores puedan jugar en ligas profesionales como Italia, Alemania, Estados Unidos y luego representan a España. También muchos son de los Marlins de Tenerife, nuestro mejor club", zanja. Luis Guillorme, llegó a jugar en los Mets de la MLS y ahora juega en la liga profesional mexicana.

articles.title: Mohamed Salah sets Turkish Super Lig record for Trabzonspor
articles.summary: Salah becomes first player with 10 goal contributions, seven goals and three assists after Trabzonspor beat Samsunspor.
articles.body:
Mohamed Salah has set a new record in Turkiye’s top flight of club football, becoming the first player to have 10 goal contributions in his first seven games for Trabzonspor in the Turkish Super Lig.

The Egyptian icon provided an assist in Trabzonspor’s 3-0 win over Samsunspor on Saturday and took his goal-assist tally to three in addition to his seven goals in as many fixtures in a prolific start to his career in Turkiye since his move from Liverpool.

The 10 goal contributions in seven games are a record for any player in the Super Lig.

The 34-year-old joined the Turkish side from the English Premier League club in August on a two-year contract in what was then seen as a surprise move.

Salah was a free agent after leaving the Anfield club at the end of the last season in English football.

When his move to Trabzonspor was completed, Salah was greeted by throngs of fans on his arrival in Istanbul.

The Egypt captain made his competitive ⁠debut for ⁠Trabzonspor off the bench in their Turkish Super Lig season opener against Kasimpasa, which ended in a 1-1 draw.

A month later, he scored a hat-trick and provided an assist as Trabzonspor thrashed defending champions Galatasaray 4-0 at home, handing the ⁠⁠⁠⁠Istanbul side their first defeat of the season.

Trabzonspor are seven-time Turkish champions and finished third last season.

articles.title: New WWE Survivor Series 2026 Match Card Predictions After Money in the Bank
articles.summary: More than anything, this year's polarizing WWE Money in the Bank—filled with above-average action and questionable booking decisions—set the stage for what should be an interesting installment of Survivor Series on Nov. 28.
articles.body:
More than anything, this year's polarizing WWE Money in the Bank—filled with above-average action and questionable booking decisions—set the stage for what should be an interesting installment of Survivor Series on Nov. 28.

Crown Jewel is next up on WWE's event calendar in early November, but Survivor Series has historically been the bigger show, especially since WarGames was made an annual staple at the Thanksgiving weekend classic starting in 2022.

Although the WarGames concept has become repetitive in recent years, it might actually be warranted for both the men and the women at the upcoming Survivor Series. The Bloodline and The 946 waging war on Raw as of late makes matters more exciting, while a case can also be made for the women given the current chaos surrounding the Women's World Championship.

That's in addition to the unpredictable Undisputed WWE Championship picture over on SmackDown and the targets on the backs of United States champion Trick Williams and WWE Women's champion Chelsea Green.

These are the newest match card predictions for Survivor Series 2026 in the immediate aftermath of Money in the Bank.

Women's WarGames: Judgment Day, Valkyria and Parker vs. Vaquer, Lynch, Bayley, Ruca and Vice

There's been much more faction warfare with the women on SmackDown in recent months compared to Raw, but there seems to be a stronger story that can be told with the ladies of the red brand heading into Survivor Series in WarGames.

Liv Morgan is once again the Women's World champion following her Triple Threat victory over Stephanie Vaquer and Becky Lynch at Money in the Bank. She pinned Vaquer to regain the gold and it would be boring for her and Lynch to rekindle their rivalry one-on-one, so Roxanne Perez should be built up as her next opponent.

Before Morgan and Perez can face off for the title, they must first go their separate ways, and a loss in WarGames would accelerate the process. They already have established issues with Vaquer, Lynch, Sol Ruca and Lola Vice, so all of those women (along with The Judgment Day's Raquel Rodriguez) should be a part of the bout.

If WWE is insistent on keeping the five-on-five format, Lyra Valkyria and Jaida Parker can be added to the heel team, provided that Valkyria's archrival Bayley joins the babyface squad. Parker currently has no equal counterpart in The Bloodline unless Naomi's return to the ring is imminent, but it's possible that she makes an enemy out of one of the aforementioned babyfaces in the coming weeks.

United States Championship: Trick Williams vs. Damian Priest

Trick Williams had a standout showing in the men's Money in the Bank Ladder match on Saturday night, but it wasn't quite his time to take home the briefcase. He at least has the United States Championship to fall back on, having kicked off his second stint with the star-spangled prize at Sunday Night's Main Event last month.

SmackDown's midcard scene has been quiet for the better part of the year, as there's no obvious challengers waiting in the wings for Williams at the moment. By Survivor Series, however, Damian Priest should be next in line for an opportunity.

The Archer of Infamy finally betrayed R-Truth on SmackDown in Mexico City last month and has made life miserable for his former friend in the weeks since. When they go one-on-one on the Oct. 16 edition of SmackDown, Priest should win with ease before setting his sights on the United States Championship.

It was Priest's first taste of gold upon joining WWE's main roster in 2021, a title he held for over six months and restored prestige to. It wouldn't be out of the realm of possibility for him to win it back on a stage as special as Survivor Series.

Undisputed WWE Championship: Sami Zayn vs. CM Punk vs. Kevin Owens

Everyone at the top of the card on SmackDown has been in hot pursuit of the Undisputed WWE Championship since SummerSlam. Current champ Sami Zayn has no clear number one contender coming out of Money in the Bank, but two names in particular would make the most sense to challenge for it in a Triple Threat at Survivor Series.

As seen on the final SmackDown before Money in the Bank, CM Punk and Kevin Owens have just as much of an issue with Zayn as they do with each other. Although they failed to emerge from the event with the opportunistic briefcase, they can easily contend for the title without it.

Survivor Series isn't for another month and a half, so WWE would have to stretch out the ongoing rivalry between the three of them until then, but it's certainly possible if Zayn's focus is going to be on Roman Reigns until their expected champion vs. champion clash at Crown Jewel.

Punk and Owens' rivalry can continue to simmer in the meantime, making for a marquee matchup come Survivor Series with Zayn as the defending champion. The best part is that any of them could realistically win, or that the title could change hands before then given how volatile the state of SmackDown has been in 2026.

WWE Women's Championship: Chelsea Green vs. Tiffany Stratton

Of everyone involved in the women's Money in the Bank Ladder match, WWE went with the least compelling option as the winner in Tiffany Stratton. She's undoubtedly an incredible talent, but as a former WWE Women's champion and Ms. Money in the Bank, history did not need to repeat itself.

The writing has been on the wall for Chelsea Green since she captured the WWE Women's Championship at SummerSlam. It's no coincidence that she and Stratton became much closer as friends shortly afterward, and it's because Stratton is determined to drop the boom on Green when she least expects it to take her title.

Stratton winning the Money in the Bank briefcase on Saturday simply confirmed that looming reality, and it won't be long before it comes to fruition.

Green first has to dispose of Nikki Bella, who owns a victory over Paige and has expressed interest in fighting for the WWE Women's title. Once Green gets past the WWE Hall of Famer, Stratton can cash in on Green and cement her heel turn by beating her for the belt.

A rematch between the two would be a fine addition to the Survivor Series card. If the Women's World champion is wrapped up in WarGames, this would ensure one of the two women's world title holders is defending on the show.

Men's WarGames: The 946, LA Knight and Oba Femi vs. The Bloodline and Solo Sikoa

More often than not, The Bloodline have been a constant in WarGames at Survivor Series since 2022 and this year may be no exception.

The Bloodline have been running rampant on Raw since WrestleMania 42 and have only bolstered their dominance by adding Jacob Fatu to their ranks in the spring. Simultaneously, they've made enemies out of LA Knight, Solo Sikoa and The 946, so there's any number of directions WWE can go in with WarGames this year.

The Bloodline's team would of course consist of Roman Reigns, The Usos and Fatu. Sikoa would be a logical ally for them based on his decision to team with them for the six-man tag team match on Monday's Raw.

The 946 would fill out three spots on the opposing team, and if they had to recruit two more partners, Knight and Oba Femi would be fine choices. Knight just lost to Reigns at Money in the Bank and might feel betrayed by Sikoa choosing to do anything with The Bloodline, while Femi wants to make a major statement by stepping up to the World Heavyweight champion.

A three-on-three-on-three format would work as well with The Bloodline battling The 946 and the trio of Knight, Sikoa and the returning Seth Rollins, but if five-on-five remains the rule, these are the most likely lineups for the multi-man mayhem that awaits WarGames.

Graham Mirmina, aka Graham "GSM" Matthews, has specialized in sports and entertainment writing since 2010. Visit his website, WrestleRant , and subscribe to his YouTube channel for more wrestling-related content.

articles.title: Can the Rangers Survive Without Igor Shesterkin? Analysis, Trade Options After Season-Ending Injury
articles.summary: It was fun while it lasted. The ambiance around Madison Square Garden (Knicks aside) had been warm for the first time in three years following a 4-1 start to the New York Rangers' season. The party came to a crashing halt on Friday night after Igor Shesterkin suffered a serious injury.
articles.body:
It was fun while it lasted. The ambiance around Madison Square Garden (Knicks aside) had been warm for the first time in three years following a 4-1 start to the New York Rangers' season. The party came to a crashing halt on Friday night after Igor Shesterkin suffered a serious injury.

Rangers fans were holding their breath, hoping for merely "bad" news. They got terrible news instead. Their best player's season is over.

A memory that may inspire hope is Henrik Lundqvist's fluke throat injury on Jan. 31, 2015. His absence for what would be 25 games was presumed to be a catastrophe. Alas, backup goaltender Cam Talbot took a monumental load and won 16 of 23 games with a .929 save percentage. The Rangers won the Presidents' Trophy. Could history repeat?

Don't bet on it. As great as Henrik Lundqvist was, the 2014-15 Rangers were an excellent team on other merits. At the time of the injury, they were playing like a top-five NHL team. They had a Rocket Richard contender in Rick Nash and arguably the best third line in hockey.

The praise of the Rangers' early play this season is absolutely valid. The full lineup has bought into a style of play that creates low-event hockey through waves of forecheck pressure, aggressive defender movement, and protection of middle ice. What this amounted to was fairly average play on the whole.

The ability to grind teams down and frustrate them depended on Shesterkin as the Final Boss. In his four full games, Shesterkin saved 3.41 goals above expected, or .85 goals per game. He was also the only reason the Rangers were tied with Washington prior to his injury.

Without him, it's difficult to point to a strength for this team. Goals are going to be hard to come by. There's no superlative talent at the top of the lineup, and the third line has struggled. The wins against the Red Wings and Islanders were good building blocks but, as the Capitals reminded everyone, the Rangers have far tougher tests on the schedule.

Sometimes, opportunity is random. Two weeks ago, the Rangers were willing to lose goaltending prospect Dylan Garand for free via waivers . Now, they're depending on him to save the season.

Nobody can fault the Rangers' front office for both Shesterkin and Joonas Korpisalo getting injured in the same window. That's rotten luck. They can be faulted for adjacent failures that accentuate the risks of the current moment.

When Shesterkin got injured in January last season, it was an opportunity to see what they had in Garand. The Rangers were already out of the playoff picture. Jonathan Quick was headed to retirement. The team was struggling and had little to lose and plenty to gain by handing a run of games to their best goaltending prospect. If he succeeded, then they would be able to pencil him in for the backup role in 2026-27. If not, then they'd know he's not a solution and the goaltending depth chart needed work.

Instead? They went to Spencer Martin, who was struggling in the AHL. He was arguably the worst goaltender in the NHL last season over his six games. Down the stretch, they prioritized a send-off for Jonathan Quick.

The Rangers had multiple opportunities to see if Garand could sink or swim in the NHL under their own terms and in a less consequential situation. Now, they have no choice, and Garand's trial will be an attempt to replace the best goaltender in the world while the team tries to save its season. No pressure!

Garand is a competitor, at least. Both on the ice, but more generally, as a mindset. He has performed well in different suboptimal environments. He faced a lot of shots for Kamloops in the WHL. The ice was often tilted towards him in Hartford. He responded to a rollercoaster week and spontaneous call-up with a shutout in Detroit, then filled in admirably mid-game against Washington.

Garand has, if nothing else, the guts to meet the moment. The silver lining is that the Rangers, who inexplicably refused to give Garand his chance, now have no choice. If he plays well, then it may at least answer some questions.

Will the Rangers Survive or Be Forced to Punt on This Season?

Even with Shesterkin, the Rangers were roughly a coin flip to make the playoffs and maybe had the upside to win a first-round series. Without him? Forget it. This is not a team headed for the lottery — playoffs may even still be within reach — but any belief that this team is capable of making some real noise is delusional.

To that end, the best move for the Rangers is probably to take this on the chin, grin and bear it for the rest of the season, sell at the deadline, and regroup. Sometimes, outside forces decide it's just not your year.

It must have been easy for Panthers GM Bill Zito to sell that idea to ownership and fans last season when Sacha Barkov and Matthew Tkachuk went down. The Panthers were still basking in the glow of back-to-back Stanley Cups.

Rangers GM Chris Drury has no such equity. The 24-25 and 25-26 seasons were unquestionably the two most pathetic seasons this franchise has experienced in the Salary Cap era. His perception among the fanbase could not be lower, while his standing with his new boss is unknown. There is significant pressure for this team to be demonstrably competitive.

This is dangerous territory for a franchise. An executive fighting to keep his or her job can be motivated to save today by borrowing from the future at a high interest rate. If it fails, you likely won't be around to deal with the consequences, anyway.

It is self-evidently not in the organization's best interest to throw more assets away in a desperate attempt to carry on as usual.

The Rangers are going to have to add someone to the depth chart to, at the very least, eat minutes while Korpisalo sits. It's not fair to saddle Garand with the whole load; this group of Rangers deserves a chance to at least salvage the season, and the development of critical young players will depend partially on a baseline competency in net.

Veteran Eric Comrie, stashed in the AHL by San Jose, is one option. He's been an above-average backup goaltender in the NHL over the last few seasons, with stops in Buffalo and Winnipeg.

In a similar vein, Dave Rittich had a strong season on Long Island last season. The Devils signed him to compete for the backup job this training camp, only to demote him and claim goaltender Remi Poirier off waivers. NJ won't rush to help out the Rangers, but if he's being offered an NHL position, the Devils will have a tough time convincing him to accept the fourth-string role.

I'd look at Los Angeles' Erik Portillo. Once a top NCAA goaltender, he's fallen to fourth on the LA depth chart. The 6'6" goaltender had a strong 2025-26 season in the AHL.

The Rangers brought Alexander Smolin, 23, into development camp this past summer. The Russian goaltender has a .939 save percentage through 12 games in the KHL this season. Is it possible to find a way to bring him over?

What Drury should avoid is a desperation trade to save the season. No, Jordan Binnington, Mackenzie Blackwood, or Samuel Montembeault will not change the perception of a sunk season. Throwing away mid-round draft picks in a desperate hope to scratch and claw to 94 points and a first-round exit is not how a Stanley Cup is won.

There will be other opportunities. A Connor Hellebuyck trade may create a cascade effect. Teams may promote a prospect and look to dump a backup. The Rangers will have options.

articles.title: 5 WWE Matches Money in the Bank Just Made Possible
articles.summary: WWE produced one of its most popular premium live events of the calendar year, Saturday night in New Orleans, in Money in the Bank, from which the company has a handful of matches it can book moving forward.
articles.body:
WWE produced one of its most popular premium live events of the calendar year, Saturday night in New Orleans, in Money in the Bank, from which the company has a handful of matches it can book moving forward.

From a hellish grudge match featuring hatred both on and off the screen to a world title match featuring the biggest star of today and the face of the future, they are matches with long-reaching effects on the WWE product.

Punk vs. Owens was a match that anyone paying even the slightest bit of attention to the WWE product knew was coming. It was even more obvious after a Money in the Bank Ladder Match that saw them lose the chance to cash in and become champion by costing each other the victory.

Owens and Punk have a genuine hatred for each other that plays well on TV, feels believable, and has yet to reach a definitive conclusion.

Emerging from the latest premium live event, it is a program destined to wrap up in a high-profile match-up between them, potentially with high stakes, ala a title match awaiting the winner.

The Young OG and The Badass had an intense, physical match-up on the lead-in to Money in the Bank, and the unsettled issues between them are only heating up following the events of Saturday night's show.

First, Breakker injured Evans with a vicious spear. Then, the babyface rode an ambulance back into the arena, thereby distracting his rival just long enough to spoil his momentum.

From there, they engaged in a hard-hitting back-and-forth that culminated in one of the damnedest spots in Money in the Bank history as Evans was pushed off a ladder and crashed through the roof of an ambulance.

One simply does not have that much interaction with no intention of paying it off in a one-on-one battle that, hopefully, gives the Young OG enough rub to make a main event run possible.

Much has been made of the decision to have Stratton win her second Money in the Bank briefcase, becoming just the second woman to do so, but there is a precedent for it based on the storyline playing out each week on SmackDown.

Stratton has become increasingly friendly with WWE Women's Champion Chelsea Green, despite initial hesitancy to align herself with the Hot Mess.

Now, she has a briefcase that guarantees her a title shot whenever she wants.

What better way to turn Stratton back heel than by having her betray the beloved Green and take her title from her? That makes the spoiled rich girl the hated heel she was intended to be and drums up further sympathy for Green.

Ironically enough, the same fans denouncing that creative idea are the ones who were championing Roxanne Perez to win the briefcase, then do the same thing to Liv Morgan, despite the teases of dissension within Judgment Day not being omnipresent in weeks.

Liv Morgan may have regained the Women's World Championship, but it was the intensified dislike between Vaquer and Lynch that was most notable in Saturday's Triple Threat Match.

The two babyfaces' inability to set aside their issues led to La Primera sending The Man into a table at ringside, a distraction that allowed Morgan to recover and deliver Oblivion to Vaquer for the win.

Lynch and Vaquer must settle their differences, and a marquee match-up between two of the best wrestlers on the planet feels like an appropriate way to do so. Booking them go to the ring without any distractions or unnecessary overbooking, letting them beat each other up, and having the best woman emerge victorious is something the WWE Universe will absolutely get behind.

Based on what happened Saturday, it is no longer a dream match. Instead, it is a creative must.

If you did no already know that the direction for this year's WrestleMania 43 is Oba Femi vs. Roman Reigns for the World Heavyweight Championship, you do after Saturday's Money in the Bank post-show.

The Ruler bested Bronson Reed in a brilliant battle of the heavyweights, during which he tossed the Auszilla around the ring with ease and eventually overcame a back injury and interference from The Vision to earn the win.

After the show, Femi joined the post-show panel and, amid a chant of "OTC" from the fans in New Orleans, Femi issued a warning to Reigns, telling him there was no more running and that time is running out.

It is the biggest, freshest main event match WWE can produce and one that will result in the Ruler's coronation as the company's next face.

articles.title: Kenya’s Eliud Kipchoge wins his first marathon in three years in Melbourne
articles.summary: Kipchoge is attempting ⁠⁠to run a marathon on all seven continents over two years as part of his ‘World Tour’ campaign.
articles.body:
Two-time Olympic champion Eliud Kipchoge has won his first marathon in three years, with the Kenyan great cruising to victory in Melbourne, Australia.

The most decorated marathoner in history crossed the finish line in 2 hours, 9 minutes and 10 seconds, two seconds under the race record, on Sunday.

It was his first victory over the distance since Berlin in 2023 and part of his “World Tour” to raise funds for causes he believes in.

The 41-year-old former world record-holder announced in 2025 that he planned to complete marathons on all seven continents, including Antarctica, over two years.

Melbourne was the third stop after South Africa and Brazil.

He broke away inside the last 10km on a course that partly used the Australian Formula One track at Albert Park and finished inside the iconic Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG).

“On the course, it was really wonderful; I enjoyed seeing people standing, cheering, and shouting my name,” Kipchoge said, looking fresh at the finish.

Kipchoge would have gone faster, but he slowed down at the MCG, waving to fans.

“It was actually different – running on a beautiful course, but also running on the Formula One track, and above all else, finishing on a cricket ground,” he added.

“I believe that my body is still peaking – still able to compete with the next generation.

“The oldest athlete ⁠⁠is still competing, but I am happy to run with the Gen Zs. I [increased] the pace after 30km to ⁠⁠see whether I can run well and beat the [race record]. My ⁠⁠plan went well.”

Australian Thomas ⁠⁠Do Canto finished second behind Kipchoge at 2:10:35, while compatriot Reece Edwards was third at 2:14:33.

New Zealand’s Camille French ‌‌won the women’s race in 2:28:25, followed by Australian Sinead Diver at 2:28:49 and Nichola Sheridan ‌‌of ‌‌Ireland at 2:29:13.

articles.title: Jalen Brunson’s Knicks return shouldn’t become a workload gamble
articles.summary: Jalen Brunson has scored 25 points in 35 preseason minutes and made half of his shots. The Knicks are getting […]
articles.body:
Jalen Brunson has scored 25 points in 35 preseason minutes and made half of his shots. The Knicks are getting a productive version of their captain again. Their 0-2 exhibition record isn't a reason to rush him into a regular-season workload.

I'd keep the progression deliberate. Brunson went from 15 minutes in Philadelphia on Monday to 20 against Washington on Thursday. That's an increase already, and the next step should serve his preparation rather than the urge to make the preseason results look more respectable.

He is fully cleared after July surgery on his left wrist, as he confirmed at Media Day. This isn't a report of a medical restriction or a setback. Clearance means he can play; it doesn't require the Knicks to prove his readiness with a long night in a game that won't affect the standings.

The Knicks have seen the scoring they needed to see

Brunson scored 12 points on 4-for-8 shooting in the opener, then 13 on 6-for-12 against the Wizards. He had three assists in each game. Those are encouraging early returns for a player whose summer included both a championship run and a procedure on his shooting-side wrist.

The perimeter shooting hasn't been as sharp: three makes in 11 attempts from beyond the arc across the two games. I wouldn't treat that as evidence of a wrist issue when no such problem has been reported. It is a shooting result over two exhibitions, not a diagnosis.

There are basketball reasons to give him more work. Mike Brown needs his first group to regain timing, and the Knicks have had turnovers and uneven offensive stretches. The starters played around 20 minutes Thursday after shorter appearances in the opener. Brunson's next sessions should include enough time with those teammates to work through real possessions.

A rehearsal doesn't need to become a marathon

I'd rather see Brown extend one controlled stretch with the regular group than keep Brunson on the floor simply because New York is chasing an exhibition win. The aim is to prepare the offense: get the spacing right, make the next pass sooner and build the timing between the ball handler and his screeners.

The reasonable counterargument is conditioning. Brief appearances won't fully prepare a player for the demands of opening night, and a familiar starting unit still needs game-speed repetitions. That's a case for increasing minutes thoughtfully across the remaining schedule, not freezing Brunson at 15 minutes indefinitely.

The next preseason game is Monday against Minnesota. Brown can use it to test a slightly longer first-team stretch and then evaluate how that work carried over. The exact workload belongs to the coaches, player and medical staff; there is no public minutes cap to quote here.

For now, 25 points on 50 percent shooting is a better development than either loss is a concern. I'd spend the remaining preseason getting Brunson ready for the games that count, not asking him to rescue the ones that don't.

articles.title: Anthony Volpe sounds fed up, and the Yankees need to listen
articles.summary: “Enough’s enough” was the part of Anthony Volpe’s postgame response that stuck with me. Speaking after Wednesday’s elimination, the Yankees […]
articles.body:
"Enough's enough" was the part of Anthony Volpe's postgame response that stuck with me. Speaking after Wednesday's elimination, the Yankees infielder described the frustration of another disappointing season ending, as reported by Ronald Blum of the Associated Press . He wasn't asking anyone to feel sorry for him.

I like hearing that from a player whose own season was hardly comfortable. The useful response isn't to hand Volpe his old shortstop job back. It's to give him a clear chance to earn a different everyday role, with an honest explanation of what has to improve.

That distinction gets lost when a good quote becomes a referendum on whether somebody cares enough. Volpe was talking about losing, not publicly blaming his manager or teammates. His frustration can be genuine without becoming proof that his bat is fixed.

The Yankees have to judge the whole season

Volpe finished the regular season batting .245 with a .321 on-base percentage and .336 slugging percentage. He hit two home runs in 246 plate appearances. A .657 OPS doesn't earn an automatic place in the middle of an infield just because the player handled adversity well.

Wednesday also supplied a reason not to dismiss him. Starting at second base in place of Jazz Chisholm Jr. , he had an infield hit and an RBI double. The double initially appeared to be a tying home run before replay determined fan interference had affected the play. The final ruling matters: it wasn't a home run taken away despite clearing the wall on its own.

The Yankees needed offense, and Volpe contributed in an elimination game. That deserves credit. It doesn't erase the quieter nights that made his place on the team uncertain in the first place.

His move beyond shortstop is already underway. He returned to the majors in September playing second base, after working at other infield positions in Triple-A. George Lombard Jr. is part of the club's shortstop picture now. A spring competition shouldn't require undoing that development merely to restore the arrangement Volpe had before his demotion.

Give him an assignment, not another vague promise

I'd prepare Volpe for a serious second-base competition and keep his third-base work going. The Yankees haven't announced that plan, and it depends on what happens with Chisholm and the rest of the infield this winter.

A versatile reserve role is a reasonable alternative if a better everyday second baseman is available. There is nothing insulting about asking Volpe to make that job difficult to take from him. The club shouldn't promise a starting position that his production hasn't secured, then spend another summer struggling to explain why the promise still stands.

What I'd ask for is specific: more extra-base damage without giving away the on-base percentage, dependable work at the position he's actually competing for, and a stretch of good at-bats that lasts beyond a memorable return or one playoff game. Those are baseball standards he can work toward.

Volpe sounded tired of ending seasons this way. By spring, the Yankees should be able to tell him exactly how they expect him to help change it.

articles.title: 49ers vs. Seahawks: How to watch, game time, and betting odds
articles.summary: The biggest game of the season, thus far. Here come the Seahawks
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers will be playing their most important game yet this year in Week 5 as they travel to face the Seattle Seahawks. This can be seen as "Part 2" of a test for the 49ers offense going up against respectable defenses. The Denver Broncos were first, and might not have been the best test since several players were injured. The Seattle Seahawks are a defense that has given the 49ers fits in the past. Brock Purdy has entered the MVP conversation, and this game can make or break that conversation continuing past Week 5. This will be an afternoon game on Fox. Kevin Burkhardt has the play-by-play, and Tom Brady will be doing color.

The 4-0 49ers head to Seattle 2-0 in their division. A win here could impact the NFC West as a whole. For the 49ers specifically, starting the season 3-0 in a competitive NFC West is something anyone would sign up for.

Last week, the 49ers faced the Broncos, and that defense gave the 49ers all they could handle for three quarters. Brock Purdy eventually found the cracks and put the game out of reach, but it was a nail-biter for most of the game. Most of that was due to an inept Broncos offense, which left several plays on the field.

The Seahawks didn't leave plays on the field in their game last week; rather, they just took their foot off the gas, letting the Los Angeles Chargers back into things when it should have been over. Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert threw a costly interception at the very end, but the Seahawks were definitely playing with their food towards the end of the game. They have only one loss on the year, coming against the Washington Commanders. The 49ers start a difficult stretch of their schedule, traveling to face the Broncos, hosting the Kansas City Chiefs, and then facing the Chicago Bears. The 49ers can happily get them prepped up for that schedule by handing them another "L".

In 2025, the 49ers failed to score a single touchdown against the Seahawks in their last two meetings. This was due to the injury bug decimating the roster and the Seahawks defense having Shanahan's number. The biggest issue was the wide receivers, but the 49ers have improved a lot. Brock Purdy has yet to take a sack in 2026, so the offensive line is much improved from last year as well. We've seen nothing but good things from the 49ers thus far, but to be the man, you gotta beat the man. In this case, with the 49ers being at the top of several power rankings, they need to prove that legitimacy by beating the reigning Super Bowl champions.

The 49ers will be without fullback Kyle Juszczyk, who suffered a knee sprain last week. They also will be without defensive lineman Nick Bosa (calf), James Thompson (ankle), and safety Marques Sigle. Mykel Williams, who began the season on the PUP list, will start his first game for 2026 after returning from a knee injury. However, he is listed as questionable along with cornerback Upton Stout (shoulder).

The Seahawks will be without running back Zach Charbonnet, cornerback Julian Neal (hamstring), and linebacker Chazz Surratt (calf). Running back George Holani (ribs) and wide receiver Irvin Charles (knee) are questionable.

articles.title: Have McCabe and Mead taken Arsenal Women’s fire with them?
articles.summary: Arsenal Women entered the new season with high expectations, but five Women’s Super League matches later, the picture looks rather different.Just one victory...
articles.body:
Arsenal Women entered the new season with high expectations, but five Women's Super League matches later, the picture looks rather different.

Just one victory, five points from a possible fifteen and a ten-point gap to leaders Manchester City have left Renée Slegers with plenty to think about during the international break.

There is no shortage of quality in this Arsenal squad. So why are the results not reflecting the talent available?

Perhaps the problem goes beyond formations, tactics and team selection. Have Arsenal lost some of the competitive edge that once made them such difficult opponents?

Has Arsenal lost some of its fighting spirit?

An interesting article in The Guardian recently raised the question of whether Arsenal are simply too nice to compete consistently with Manchester City and Chelsea.

The departures of Katie McCabe and Beth Mead during the summer removed two players who brought considerable personality, experience and determination to the dressing room.

McCabe, in particular, was never afraid of a confrontation or a physical challenge. Her fiery approach occasionally landed her in trouble, but she brought an intensity that opponents could hardly ignore.

Mead offered a different kind of leadership, combining experience with the confidence to take responsibility in difficult moments.

As we discussed when examining Arsenal Women's extensive summer squad overhaul , integrating so many new faces was always going to take time.

However, replacing talent is one thing. Replacing established personalities and the influence they have on a team is another.

Can Renée Slegers restore Arsenal's competitive edge?

Arsenal's recent performances have highlighted some worrying patterns.

Against Chelsea, the Gunners created opportunities but failed to convert them. Against Manchester City, they twice took the lead before eventually losing 4-2.

Our latest Arsenal Women Weekly Roundup also highlighted the disappointment of surrendering a two-goal advantage against Paris FC in Europe.

These are different matches, but they raise similar questions about composure, determination and the ability to manage difficult moments.

Of course, fighting spirit does not necessarily mean aggressive tackling or collecting yellow cards. Arsenal have experienced leaders in Leah Williamson and Kim Little, while Georgia Stanway brings her own competitive qualities.

The challenge for Slegers is finding a way to turn those individual strengths into a collective resilience that lasts for ninety minutes.

The international break offers an opportunity for reflection, even with several players away representing their countries.

With the WSL title race already looking increasingly difficult, Arsenal cannot afford many more setbacks when domestic football resumes.

Perhaps this is not about Arsenal being too nice. Perhaps it is about rediscovering the hunger, confidence and ruthlessness that made them European champions .

What do you think, Gooners? Have Arsenal Women lost some of their fighting spirit following the summer departures, or are we simply seeing the growing pains of a significantly reshaped squad? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below.

articles.title: Kim Kardashian teases Martin Brundle on F1 grid in Singapore: ‘Did we get off on the wrong foot?’
articles.summary: Kardashian is in Singapore to support Lewis Hamilton, four months on from her appearance in Monaco
articles.body:
Kim Kardashian joked with Martin Brundle on the F1 grid in Singapore , asking the Sky broadcaster four months on from shunning him in Monaco: "Did we get off on the wrong foot?"

Kardashian is supporting boyfriend Lewis Hamilton in Singapore this weekend, who started Sunday's grand prix third on the grid.

At the Monaco GP in June, American celebrity Kardashian ignored Brundle's request to speak on the grid, with a few questions falling on deaf ears.

Yet ahead of F1's original "night race" in the Asian city-state on Sunday, Kardashian was more accommodating. As Brundle approached again with his microphone, she said: "Martin… did I not know the rules? Did we get off on the wrong foot?!"

Brundle smiled and replied: "Not it's absolutely fine! Lovely to see you again at a grand prix. What do you think of our crazy world of Formula 1?"

Kardashian said: "I think it's amazing and fun and wild and something I've never seen before, it's amazing."

When asked about Hamilton's strong form and season, she added: "I'm just praying for the best tonight. He's very confident and so am I – got to pray for the best!"

Sky Sports F1 broadcaster Brundle, known for his amusing encounters with celebrities on the grid, had a bizarre encounter with Jimmy Fallon in Miami in May when the American talk show host bit his microphone .

Brundle, who had a mix-up with Lewis Capaldi's brother in Singapore last year and was shunned by Usher in Saudi Arabia, also had a run-in with Kylian Mbappe's bodyguard in 2024 in Monaco, saying "I'm in charge here", when trying to conduct an interview with the France and Real Madrid star.

In Brazil in November 2023, Brundle bumped into American rapper Machine Gun Kelly and an odd interview occurred, in which the American rapper fiddled with Brundle's poppy, asked him to play the air guitar and put his thumb down to the camera at the end.

Brundle also endured hilarious encounters with DJ Khaled and Pharrell Williams in Miami in 2022, as well as a slightly frosty exchange with Cara Delevingne at Silverstone three years ago, in which the model refused to talk to the broadcaster.

articles.title: What Happened to DeVonta Smith? Latest Update on Eagles Star’s Injury and Why He’s Not Playing in Week 5 vs. Jaguars
articles.summary: The 2-2 Philadelphia Eagles will be looking to get their season back on track when they face the 3-1 Jacksonville Jaguars in London on Sunday. Philadelphia e...
articles.body:
The 2-2 Philadelphia Eagles will be looking to get their season back on track when they face the 3-1 Jacksonville Jaguars in London on Sunday. Philadelphia enters the Week 5 matchup hoping to snap a frustrating two-game losing streak and regain some momentum.

However, the task will be tougher with the Eagles shorthanded at wide receiver, as DeVonta Smith is among the notable players ruled out for the game.

Why Is DeVonta Smith Ruled Out For Week 5?

Smith will miss Philadelphia's game against Jacksonville because of a lingering hamstring injury. The wide receiver did not participate in any of the Eagles' three practices this week, suggesting he has made little progress toward a return.

Smith was spotted running on a side field Thursday before continuing his rehabilitation Friday. While those activities suggested he was making progress, it was not enough to put him in contention for Sunday's game.

The hamstring issue is not new for Smith, who missed a significant portion of Philadelphia's training camp with the same injury. He also sat out the Eagles' Week 4 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.

Smith played every offensive snap in Philadelphia's 27-7 loss to the Chicago Bears in Week 3. However, the injury kept him out of practice ahead of the Rams game, and he has yet to return to full participation.

Smith's absence is particularly concerning for Philadelphia, which will also be without Hollywood Brown because of an ankle injury.

With both receivers sidelined for the London game, the Eagles will have to turn to Elijah Moore, Dontayvion Wicks, Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, and Britain Covey for additional options in the passing game.

When Will DeVonta Smith Be Able To Play?

There is no confirmed timetable for the 27-year-old's return. His recovery will likely depend on how his hamstring responds to rehabilitation and whether he can resume practicing in the coming days.

The Eagles will need to monitor Smith's progress closely before determining whether he can return for their Week 6 game against the Carolina Panthers.

Smith has made a solid start to the 2026 season, catching 19 of 27 targets for 235 receiving yards and one touchdown in three games.

He currently ranks No. 27 with a PFN WR Impact Score of 76.2.

When healthy, Smith remains a key option in Philadelphia's passing attack, making his continued absence a significant blow to the offense.

articles.title: Pundit knows exactly where Juventus needs to improve on as a team
articles.summary: Juventus is keen to become the top team in Serie A again, and they know this will be an important season to make that happen as they look to win the Scudetto...
articles.body:
Juventus is keen to become the top team in Serie A again, and they know this will be an important season to make that happen as they look to win the Scudetto again for the first time since 2020. Juve has a strong squad and believes they can make the top four at the end of this season, which will be a great step towards them winning another league title.

They do not need to be Italian champions when this season ends, but if they do well and make progress from the last term, this could be the season that they will edge ever closer and then become champions next term. It is still very much a building site at the Allianz Stadium, and Juve is doing its best to ensure the team is in fine shape and wins some trophies as soon as they can.

Their rebuild is taking shape, and they can say they have sorted out the defence, but there are other spots on the team that remain questionable. Massimo Bonini has discussed where they need to improve and said via Tuttojuve :

"I expect them to grow, especially to be more united. Because maybe it's a team that did, yes, against Atalanta, a great performance, but in the others it left a bit to be desired.

"In the sense that maybe they get goals still demonstrating a team with not so much tactical balance. It needs to grow in compactness and be more team. But I think one thing: that Juventus has players with great talent. They just need to become more of a team."

(Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)

Bonini's comments highlight the need for greater cohesion, with tactical balance a key area for improvement. The squad's talent is undeniable, but turning that into consistent results requires a collective effort. The manager's task is to mould these individuals into a cohesive unit.

Juventus's ambitions are clear, and the club is working towards a long-term vision. The defence has been strengthened, but midfield and attack still need refinement. The coming months will show whether the team can find that balance.

Supporters will hope the side can build on positives like the Atalanta performance , while addressing the inconsistencies. The Scudetto may be a stretch this term, but progress towards it is the goal. Bonini's insights reflect the challenges ahead, and the club's response will be crucial.

articles.title: Ugly scene unfolds at Bryant-Denny Stadium as Georgia players leave field
articles.summary: Georgia’s players put their helmets back on before they reached the tunnel at Bryant-Denny Stadium on Saturday night, after Alabama fans started throwing bot...
articles.body:
Georgia's players put their helmets back on before they reached the tunnel at Bryant-Denny Stadium on Saturday night, after Alabama fans started throwing bottles and cans at them following the Bulldogs' 20-17 win. The victory moved No. 2 Georgia to 6-0 and handed No. 6 Alabama its first loss of the season.

Dozens of items landed in the Alabama end zone, and a water bottle came down near a cheerleader, who stepped back to avoid it. WSB-TV's Alison Mastrangelo posted video of the exit.

"Georgia players were being told by coaches to put their helmets on as they were leaving the field," Mastrangelo wrote. "Upset Alabama fans were throwing bottles and cans at the players and on the field."

The crowd had turned on the officials during Alabama's final drive. Keelon Russell took a deep shot toward Rico Scott, who was hit going for the ball, and no pass interference flag came out. Fans booed for the rest of the game. Russell was sacked on the next snap, which pushed Alabama out of field goal range and forced a punt.

Georgia took over with 3:10 left, and a personal foul on cornerback Dijon Lee Jr. on third-and-2 gave the Bulldogs the first down they needed to kneel out the clock.

"We can't put the game in the situation where the officials come into play. We got to control the things we control," Kalen DeBoer said of the no-call.

Georgia was on the receiving end of a similar scene two years ago. On Oct. 19, 2024, Texas fans threw water bottles and trash onto the field in Austin after a pass interference penalty briefly wiped out a Jahdae Barron interception against Georgia. Officials reversed the call, and the SEC fined Texas $250,000 the next day.

"The throwing of debris and resulting interruption of play that took place Saturday night cannot be part of any SEC event," SEC commissioner Greg Sankey said at the time.

The league also required Texas to identify and suspend the fans responsible and to review its alcohol policies, with alcohol sales at risk if the school failed to comply.

The Austin debris stopped a game in progress. Saturday's came after the clock ran out, with visiting players walking toward the tunnel, which puts the safety of an opposing team at the center of any review the conference opens.

Alabama had its own bottles thrown at it in Baton Rouge in November 2024, when the SEC fined LSU $250,000 . No statement from the SEC or Alabama on Saturday's scene had been reported as of this report.

articles.title: UConn topples Temple, 34-20
articles.summary: The UConn Huskies (3-3) took down the Temple Owls, 34-20, before heading into their bye week. Quarterback Kalieb Osborne completed an efficient 17 of 23 (73....
articles.body:
The UConn Huskies (3-3) took down the Temple Owls, 34-20, before heading into their bye week.

Quarterback Kalieb Osborne completed an efficient 17 of 23 (73.9%) passes for 257 yards and also ran in a TD. In the backfield, Trey Cornist racked up 114 rushing yards on just seven carries, while Cyncir Bowers returned to his home state and posted 84 rushing yards with a TD and an 18-yard reception. In Kenji Christian's first game back, the senior tallied 61 yards (39 rushing, 22 passing). Defensively, the Huskies notched two fumbles that created a pair of scoring drives.

As for the Owls, Ajani Sheppard completed 19 of 25 (76%) attempts for 260 yards and a touchdown. This game started off as a shootout, ending the first quarter tied 14-14. In the second quarter, UConn separated

Both programs' offenses came out hot, but the Huskies struck first. At the 25-yard line, Osborne connected with Ryder Treadway on back-to-back plays for 52 yards, putting Connecticut in Temple's redzone. After Bowers rushed to the 12-yard line, Osborne finished the job. A linebacker was flying at him, but he stepped aside and ran in for a 7-0 lead.

In one play, the Owls tied it up as Sheppard launched a deep ball to a wide-open JoJo Bermudez for a 79-yard touchdown. On the next drive, UConn pushed the pace with a 39-yard TD run by Kenji Christian to go back ahead.

At the five-minute mark, Sheppard handed off a jet sweep to wideout Colin Chase. While the defense was preparing for the run, Chase fired to wide-open Paul Clarke.

The Huskies attempted to regain the lead, but got sacked on a 4th down attempt at the Temple 9.

On the ensuing Owls poessession, the Huskies gifted Temple a combined 30 yards (15 yards roughing the passer, 15 yards facemask), spotting the ball at the home team's 46-yard line. This led to Sheppard rushing up the middle and finding Bermudez for 32 yards. The drive stalled from there as kicker Carl Hardin hit a 26-yard field goal to take a 17-14 lead, their first of the day.

Osborne hit Treadway for 11 yards to the 44-yard line. Cornist carried the ball right and juked left, found the hole, bolted down to the 5-yard line after a 51-yard rush and finished the drive from the goal line to make the score 21-17.

Midway through the second frame, Keveun Mason pushed the Owls offense to the 44-yard line. After the two-minute timeout, Mason rushed for 18 yards and fumbled the ball. Renick Dorilas punched the ball out and Braedyn Moore pounced on it at UConn's 22-yard line.

On the first play, the offensive line shifted left, allowing Cornist to go for 44 yards. Near midfield, the drive was looking stalled. But on 4th-and-6, Osborne stayed strong under pressure to send a leading pass to Shamar Porter that he incredibly held on to. A roughing the passer penalty moved them to the goal line. A muffed snap moved them back so a Jack O'Conner field goal made it 24-17 at the break.

Coming out of the break, both squads traded punts. It wasn't until the three-minute mark that Temple scored the first points of the third quarter with a field goal. In just three passes, Sheppard advanced to the Huskies' 16-yard line, but the Owls settled for a 29-yard field goal.

Going into the fourth quarter, Temple constructed a promising drive reaching Connecticut's 39-yard line. From there, defensive lineman Shamar Riser-Pressley knocked the ball out of Sheppard's hand and K'Von Sherman recovered it. UConn capitalized on the fumble with a TD, forced a three-and-out, and then ran out the clock with Bowers and Cornist to set up another O'Connor field goal to set the final score at 34-20.

Next up, UConn will face UMass after their bye week on Friday, Oct. 23.
